title: 2026 UK ETS maritime verifier site-visit QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for maritime: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: Site visits are an important part of annual maritime UK ETS verification and without one the verifier may not be able to verify the report as satisfactory.
facts.expected_handling: Treat site-visit evidence as a verification control.

facts.source_fact: An in-person site visit takes place where monitoring and control of relevant data and information are managed.
facts.expected_handling: Bind visit scope to the data-management location.

facts.source_fact: During an in-person visit the verifier gathers evidence and tests internal processes and control procedures and may interview staff.
facts.expected_handling: Record the controls and evidence actually tested.

facts.source_fact: The verifier performs a risk analysis and decides how to conduct the site visit.
facts.expected_handling: Require documented risk basis for visit design.

facts.source_fact: The operator must allow access to sites the verifier wants to visit.
facts.expected_handling: Flag access restrictions as verification risk.

facts.source_fact: Because data may be centralised, the verifier may decide it is not necessary to visit every ship or every location where information is stored.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer missing verification merely because every vessel was not visited.

facts.source_fact: A virtual site visit can replace an in-person visit only where the verifier's risk analysis supports reasonable assurance that the annual emissions report is free from material misstatements.
facts.expected_handling: Require reasonable-assurance rationale for virtual visits.

facts.source_fact: For a virtual visit, the operator must apply to the Environment Agency with the risk analysis by 28 February in the year after the relevant scheme year.
facts.expected_handling: Track the 28 February approval application deadline.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency must approve a virtual site visit and may impose conditions such as an in-person visit in the following scheme year.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat virtual visit as valid without regulator approval.

facts.source_fact: A new risk analysis is generally not required for later scheme years if a virtual visit was approved and relevant circumstances have not changed, unless approval conditions require it.
facts.expected_handling: Reuse prior analysis only where conditions and circumstances permit.

guard_patterns.handling: Require visit evidence in verification records.
Tie visit to monitoring/control data location.
Do not require every ship where centralised evidence is sufficient.
Require EA approval for virtual site visit.
A site visit verifies reporting controls; it is not itself a vessel emissions measurement.
Flag risk, approval, access or condition conflicts.
